record.paper_title: Open problems in the theory of completely positive and copositive matrices
record.original_question: For each finite n > 2, compute the maximal angle theta_max(COP_n) and the maximal angle theta_max(PSD_n + N_n), where COP_n is the copositive cone, PSD_n is the cone of real symmetric positive semidefinite n x n matrices, N_n is the cone of real symmetric entrywise nonnegative n x n matrices, and theta_max(K) is the maximum of arccos(trace(XY)) over unit-norm X,Y in the cone K. Are these maximal angles always attained by a pair of matrices P in PSD_n and N in N_n?

evidence.quote: It remains an open question to compute θmax(COPn) as well as θmax(PSDn + Nn) for finite n > 2

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $n>2$ be an integer. Equip the space $S_n$ of real symmetric $n\times n$ matrices with the Frobenius inner product $\langle X,Y\rangle = \operatorname{tr}(XY)$ and the induced norm $\|X\| = \sqrt{\operatorname{tr}(X^2)}$. Define the following closed convex cones in $S_n$:

- $\operatorname{PSD}_n = \{X \in S_n : v^\top X v \ge 0 \text{ for all } v \in \mathbb{R}^n\}$, the cone of positive semidefinite matrices.
- $N_n = \{X \in S_n : X_{ij} \ge 0 \text{ for all } i,j\}$, the cone of symmetric entrywise nonnegative matrices.
- $\operatorname{COP}_n = \{X \in S_n : v^\top X v \ge 0 \text{ for all } v \in \mathbb{R}^n_{\ge 0}\}$, the copositive cone.
- $\operatorname{PSD}_n + N_n = \{P + N : P \in \operatorname{PSD}_n,\ N \in N_n\}$.

For a closed convex cone $K \subseteq S_n$ define its maximal angle
$$\theta_{\max}(K) = \sup\{\arccos(\operatorname{tr}(XY)) : X,Y \in K,\ \|X\|=\|Y\|=1\}.$$

(a) Determine $\theta_{\max}(\operatorname{COP}_n)$ in closed form for every finite $n > 2$.

(b) Determine $\theta_{\max}(\operatorname{PSD}_n + N_n)$ in closed form for every finite $n > 2$.

(c) Decide whether, for every finite $n > 2$, the supremum defining $\theta_{\max}(\operatorname{PSD}_n + N_n)$ is attained at a pair of unit-norm matrices of the form $X = P_1 + N_1$, $Y = P_2 + N_2$ in which the optimizing extremal pair can be chosen with one matrix in $\operatorname{PSD}_n$ and the other in $N_n$.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is generally open for finite $n>2$. The case $n=2$ was settled by Hiriart-Urruty and Seeger (2010), who showed $\theta_{\max}(\operatorname{COP}_2)=3\pi/4$. The case $n=3$ was resolved in a 2025 paper (Optimization Letters / arXiv:2501.03773), which proved $\theta_{\max}(\operatorname{COP}_3)=3\pi/4$ and characterized all extremal pairs. No closed-form results for $\theta_{\max}(\operatorname{COP}_n)$ or $\theta_{\max}(\operatorname{PSD}_n+N_n)$ are known for $n\ge 4$, and the question of attainment by a PSD/nonnegative pair remains open in general.

status_evidence.title: The maximal angle between 3×3 copositive matrices
status_evidence.snippet: θ₃ = 3π/4 and give all possible pairs of matrices achieving this maximal angle.
status_evidence.claim: The case n=3 has been solved: θ_max(COP_3)=3π/4.

status_evidence.title: On the maximal angle between copositive matrices (ELA)
status_evidence.snippet: Hiriart-Urruty and Seeger proved that the maximal angle between two 2×2 copositive matrices is (3/4)π.
status_evidence.claim: Case n=2 is solved; general n was conjectured 3π/4 but conjecture disproved (limit equals π).

status_evidence.title: Open problems in the theory of completely positive and copositive matrices (ELA)
status_evidence.snippet: It remains an open question to compute θ_max(COP_n) as well as θ_max(PSD_n+N_n) for finite n>2.
status_evidence.claim: Problem posed as open for finite n>2.
